new_findings_today.title: SEO hreflang probe methodology note -- not a site defect, but worth recording so a future run doesn't misreport it
new_findings_today.detail: This run's first pass at the SEO hreflang check used a case-sensitive regex (hreflang=") and got 0/12 matches on all sampled pages, which would have been reported as a severe new SEO regression. The actual markup is React/Next's server-rendered <link rel="alternate" hrefLang="en" .../> -- camelCase hrefLang, which is valid and equivalent to lowercase hreflang under the HTML spec (attribute names are case-insensitive) and is treated identically by browsers and crawlers. Re-running the check case-insensitively confirmed all 12/12/12/12 alternate tags present and correct. No site change needed; this is purely a probe-methodology gotcha for future QA runs (and for anyone writing a similar curl+regex SEO check).
new_findings_today.evidence: grep -io 'hreflang="[^"]*"' on en_tawang.html -- 0 matches lowercase, 3 matches case-insensitive (en/hi/x-default), all correct.
new_findings_today.recommendation: If this check is ever automated outside this session, make sure the hreflang regex/selector is case-insensitive.

business_summary.headline: The site is healthy. All 10 sampled destination pages, the homepage, and every core section loaded correctly in both English and Hindi this week, with no broken pages, no server errors, and no missing photos anywhere in the 533-destination catalog. The best news this week: a defect we've been tracking for a month -- a handful of destination names that happen to match an Indian state or union territory name (like Goa or Sikkim) not showing the right 'page not found' behavior -- turned out to have been properly fixed. Those web addresses now take visitors to a real, working state overview page instead of either a broken result or a dead end, and that fix also cleanly closed out a second, related item that had been lingering since May for the same underlying reason. We also caught and corrected a false alarm in our own checking process this week (explained below) before it could be reported as a problem that didn't actually exist -- a reminder that this check, like the site itself, benefits from being double-checked rather than trusted blindly. A small website update also went out this week with two minor database changes, neither of which visitors would notice.
traffic_lights: Every page we checked loaded correctly -- 10/10 sampled destinations, all core sections (trip planner, explore, emergency info, blog, treks, and more), both languages. Page speed was normal, with one single page loading a bit slower than usual on its first (cold) load, which is expected behavior and not a problem.

All 533 destinations in the catalog have verified emergency numbers on file -- no destination is missing this safety-critical information. The 10 destinations we sampled in detail averaged 8 working phone numbers each, all above our minimum safety threshold of 3.

All 12 pages we checked have correct titles, correct canonical links (so search engines know which version of a page is the 'real' one), correct language-alternate links, and social-preview images -- nothing for search engines to trip on. (Our own first-pass check briefly flagged a false alarm here before we caught and fixed our testing method -- the site itself was never at fault; see the note under 'About this report'.)

Hindi pages load correctly and have correct Hindi titles everywhere, with no exceptions found. On a specific subset of destination pages (the newer 'cinematic' page design, which covers about 70% of the catalog), the big on-page headline still shows in English instead of Hindi even though the rest of the page -- including the browser tab title -- is correctly in Hindi. This is a known, tracked issue, not a new one.
Destination web addresses that share a state's name

FIXED this week, after being open for about a month. The handful of destinations that happen to share a name with an Indian state or union territory (Goa, Sikkim, and similar) now correctly take visitors to a working state-overview page instead of a dead end or a broken result. A second, related tracking item that depended on this same fix also closed out cleanly as a result.

Two internal automations that run independently of the main website (a newsletter-delivery checker and the process that refreshes 'where to stay' recommendations) each have an open question from a prior week that wasn't re-investigated this run, to keep this week's check efficient. Neither affects anything a visitor sees today.
This check is meant to run daily but is actually only running once a week (every Monday) -- a configuration issue with the schedule itself, not the website. Flagged for Ashish to fix when convenient.

Couldn't check this week -- the tool we use to look at server error logs wasn't able to connect (an authentication issue with that specific tool, not a wider outage). Not an indication of a site problem, just a gap in this week's check that should resolve itself once that connection is fixed.
Subscriber count, send count, and open/click events all grew steadily week-over-week, with no signs of the list stalling, shrinking, or churning.

A small website update went live with two minor database changes. One of them lays groundwork for a new, not-yet-public feature for correcting destination details -- nothing visitors would notice yet, and nothing that changed how the live site behaves this week.
